commits.subject: fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants (#5944)

Author:     易良 <1204183885@qq.com>

    fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants (#5944)
    
    * fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants
    
    * test(core): cover shell-stagnation streak reset, fix guard-count doc
    
    Address review on #5944: the checkAlwaysOnSafeties JSDoc still said it
    enforces two guards after the shell inspection-command stagnation guard
    was added, so correct it to three.
    
    Add a regression test proving a non-inspection tool call resets the
    shell-stagnation streak to zero, which is the guard's main false-positive
    defense and was previously untested.
    
    * fix(core): exclude write-bearing git chains from stagnation bucket
    
    isGitInspectionCommand matched if any segment of a shell chain was a git
    status/diff/ls-files, so a productive chain like
    `git add . && git status && git commit` was classified as read-only
    inspection. Eight such commands would falsely trip the always-on
    shell-stagnation guard.
    
    Require every segment of the chain to be a read-only git inspection
    before bucketing. Mixed chains that also write fail open (non-inspection),
    the safe direction for an always-on halt. The #4695 loop is still caught:
    its compound case is status && diff, both read-only.
    
    * fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants
    
    * fix(core): treat path-specific git diffs as progress
    
    * test(core): cover shell stagnation guard boundaries
    
    * test(core): address shell stagnation review feedback
    
    * docs(core): sync loop guard comments

episode.title: Structured tool-contract integrity: stop varied read-only shell inspection loops

evidence_units.claim: Issue #4695 reports a long-context session in which the model repeatedly emits shell tool calls, asks for client-side repeated-call detection and a per-turn cap, and records substantial repeated-call cost before the user stops the run.

PR #5944 explicitly links Fixes #4695 and explains that varying read-only git overview commands can evade exact repeated-call detection; it defines the narrow always-on scope and the fail-open exclusions for file-specific diffs, write-bearing chains, mixed commands, and progress boundaries.
The pinned implementation ref 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da has parent 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620 and changes four files with 461 additions and 16 deletions.

The parent loop-detection service has a five-call exact same-tool-and-JSON-arguments guard and a 100-call per-turn hard cap in its always-on tier, but no shell-inspection bucket, shell streak state, or shell-specific always-on guard; action stagnation remains in the heuristic path.

The parent core client already invokes the always-on safety tier before the skipLoopDetection-gated heuristic tier, clears pending tool calls, yields LoopDetected, and returns when an always-on guard fires; before the change its comments enumerate only the exact-call guard and per-turn cap.

The pinned loop-detection service adds an eight-call shell-inspection threshold, dedicated last-key and streak state, a run_shell_command semantic bucket, shell-chain segmentation, read-only git overview classification, overview-diff operand validation, and reset behavior on nonmatching commands, Retry, and prompt reset.

The pinned core client runs the new shell stagnation check in the always-on tier before the skipLoopDetection gate; on detection it clears pending tool calls, yields LoopDetected with the last loop type, reports the error, cleans up, and returns.

The pinned telemetry enum defines SHELL_COMMAND_STAGNATION, and the non-interactive CLI maps it to a human-readable repeated-shell-inspection message and marks it as an always-on guard that cannot be disabled through model.skipLoopDetection.

The pinned service test file adds the shell-stagnation threshold and deterministic coverage for the eighth-call halt, non-inspection and Retry resets, explicit disable, write-bearing and mixed-chain exclusions, non-git exclusions, newline-separated variants, and file-specific diff exclusions.

The commit diff contains the four-file implementation/test/telemetry/CLI changes described by the episode, including the service guard, new loop type, CLI label, call-site contract comments, and regression tests.

The PR reports 72 core loop-detection tests, 57 CLI tests with one skipped, lint, typecheck, build, bundle, and a deterministic bundled-CLI E2E passing; the E2E served eight completion requests, executed seven tool results, and halted with shell_command_stagnation on the eighth request.

unresolved_questions: The PR explicitly reports no Windows or Linux local run and uses a fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint rather than a live DeepSeek endpoint, so platform-specific and provider-specific behavior remains deferred [EV-VALIDATION-PR].

The local WSL checkout and requested issue-bundle path were not readable from this execution sandbox; the extraction therefore used the public GitHub issue, PR, pinned commit, parent blob, pinned implementation blobs, call sites, tests, and PR-reported validation, and no local test rerun was performed.
